oil.summary: Crude surged Thursday, with Brent touching $96 and WTI up nearly 3%, driven squarely by geopolitical risk premium. Trump's declaration that the U.S. no longer needs an Iran deal—reversing comments made just days ago suggesting the eight-month war was nearing resolution—sparked the rally, compounded by his threat of sanctions on Iran's trading partners. Iran's simultaneous demand of seven conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz kept supply-disruption fears elevated. On the bearish side, EIA reported a 4.7 million barrel crude build for the week ending November 6, alongside gasoline and distillate builds, capping upside. Indian buyers rotating away from Russian crude toward Gulf barrels for the first time since the Iran war began signals shifting trade flows. UK sanctions on Russia's Slavneft and Ukraine drone strikes cutting Russian refining capacity by 30% add further supply-side noise. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2026 meeting.
drivers: Trump's Iran deal reversal and threatened secondary sanctions on Iran partners drove the intraday spike in Brent to $96
Bearish EIA data: crude inventories rose 4.7 million barrels w/w, with builds also in gasoline and distillates
Russia supply disruption risks escalate: Ukraine drone strikes cut refining capacity 30%, UK sanctions added on Slavneft

gas.summary: Henry Hub extended its strong weekly run, adding nearly 4% on the day to $3.343/MMBtu, now up over 13% on the week. News flow for natural gas was relatively thin today; available headlines point to two structural demand themes rather than near-term catalysts. EU LNG imports from Russia have already exceeded the full-year 2025 value with six weeks remaining before the January ban takes effect, underscoring how aggressively European buyers are front-running the cutoff. Meanwhile, China's energy regulator is pushing domestic gas turbine makers to target overseas data centers as AI-driven power demand accelerates globally. Specific storage or weather catalysts for today's move were not available in the provided data.
drivers: Henry Hub up ~4% on the day, extending a 13%+ weekly gain; specific intraday catalyst not detailed in available data
EU Russian LNG imports already exceed full-year 2025 levels ahead of the January ban, highlighting pre-ban stockpiling urgency
AI-driven power demand surge supporting longer-term gas consumption outlook as China targets global gas turbine sales to data centers

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up 0.82% to $86.12, posting a modest fourth consecutive weekly gain. The dominant thematic in power today is AI-driven electricity demand: China's push into overseas gas turbine markets targets data centers consuming ever-larger power loads, while a separate piece flags that the U.S. data center boom is forcing grid infrastructure investment. In the UK, Chancellor Healey's Budget signaled a notable policy shift away from prior net-zero commitments, with soaring electricity costs cited as the pressure point—a development worth monitoring for European carbon sentiment. Iran's Hormuz conditions remain a tail risk for gas-fired power generation costs across Europe. The lithium story out of Argentina is thematically relevant to the energy transition but had no direct carbon price impact today.
drivers: AI and data center power demand accelerating globally, underpinning long-term gas and grid infrastructure investment narratives
UK government signals a shift away from net-zero commitments citing soaring electricity costs, a potential headwind for carbon policy momentum
EUA prices quietly bid up 0.82% on the day; Strait of Hormuz uncertainty sustains risk premium on gas-fired power generation costs
